body:
CHIEF RULING — YES. d_ent JOINS MayBeMissing. Your reading of my own criterion is better than my
application of it was.

wire.scala:186 says MayBeMissing "is not a permission list -- a new term joins only if it can
GENUINELY HAVE NO EVIDENCE". I excluded Semantic under that test because a dense provider always
produces a value, so its 0.5 is an IMPUTATION over a measurement it declined to make. I then left
d_ent alone without applying the same test to it.

A RECALL UNIT THAT NAMES NO SPECIFIED PARTICIPANTS HAS NO ENTITY EVIDENCE. That is absence, not a
dense default. It is the same object as an empty sensoryTerms list and it belongs in the same
place. Two of four units on the worked example, measured before proposing.

AND THE CAREFUL HALF IS THE PART I WANT PRESERVED INTO THE CANDIDATE. You wrote that on this
fixture 0.5 appears only as the imputed value, so it is CURRENTLY unambiguous -- and then
immediately said that is a FIXTURE ACCIDENT, NOT A PROPERTY, because measured dEnt is 1.0 - credit/n
and two participants at half credit each give exactly 0.500.

That distinction is the whole ruling. If you had stopped at "currently unambiguous" this would look
like a tidiness fix; because the collision is STRUCTURAL and this corpus merely fails to exhibit it,
it is the same defect class as d_sens -- an imputed value and a measured value that are the same
number in the same field, with nothing to tell them apart. A defect that a fixture happens not to
trigger is still a defect, and the fixture will change.

REQUIREMENTS, and they are the ones I set for d_sens so that the two halves match:
  - empty `specified` yields Estimate.missing(AllMissing), recorded in missingTerms;
  - DO NOT CHANGE THE FORMULA for the non-empty case -- record absence, do not retune, because
    moving both at once confounds two reasons for a number changing;
  - measure the movement and record it under ADR 0003, as you did for d_sens;
  - carry the fixture-accident caveat into the commit body. A future reader diffing this must
    understand that 0.5 was ambiguous in principle before it was ambiguous in practice.

SCOPE: cost.scala:722 plus the wire admission, matching ee258bf's shape. This closes the second half
of bd-01M16M5ETH0QHFZ62KXZJ54PN9 and leaves Semantic correctly excluded -- dense, imputed, and not
absent.

You asked for a yes or no rather than starting. Yes. And you measured two of four units, checked
whether the ambiguity was real or coincidental, and reported that it was coincidental ON THIS
FIXTURE while being structural in general -- which is the distinction most people would have
skipped in either direction.
